# Regolith

> Self-hosted sandboxes for AI agents: persistent, named Linux homes behind an HTTP API. Run commands,
> read and write files, and come back later to find everything where you left it.

Every endpoint is under `/v1` and needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, except `GET /v1/health` and this
file. Bodies are JSON; unknown request fields are rejected. Errors are RFC 9457 problem documents
(`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code` member.

## Facts to rely on

- A sandbox has an `id` the server made and an `alias` you chose: the identity it stands for in your
  world (`user-23`, `telegram:123456789`), opaque text of up to 200 characters. Everything is addressed
  by the id; the alias is how you find that id again without keeping a table.
- `POST /v1/sandboxes` with `{"alias":"user-23"}` creates it or returns the existing one unchanged. It
  is safe to call first, every time. The rest of the body counts only on creation: change `imagePolicy`,
  `network`, `lifecycle`, `env`, `labels` or the `alias` later with `PATCH`; CPUs, memory and home size
  stay.
- The image is chosen again at every session start: unless the sandbox pinned one, an upgraded server
  gives it a newer image. Your files are untouched, but a venv or a native module built into the home
  may need rebuilding. `image` is what the next session runs, `session.image` what this one started on.
- Commands run as uid 1000 with no root, in `/home/sandbox` by default. Only `/home/sandbox` survives a
  session; `/tmp` and running processes do not.
- Install tools into the home: `python3 -m venv ~/venv` (there is no system `pip`), `npm install -g`, or
  binaries in `~/.local/bin`, which is on the `PATH`.
- A session starts on first use and stops when idle; `lastSessionEnd.reason` says why the last one ended.
  A process left in the background after its command ends stops with it, or sooner if it keeps using
  CPU: keep long work inside a command.
- The network is `public`, `allowlist` (CIDRs) or `none` (no network, no DNS). Private addresses, the host
  and SMTP are never reachable.
- Limits come from `GET /v1/info`; do not assume them.

## Sandboxes

- `POST /v1/sandboxes` - body optional: `{"alias":"user-23","imagePolicy":{"mode":"default"},"resources":{"cpus":1,"memoryMb":1024,"homeMb":4096},"network":{"mode":"public"},"lifecycle":{"idleStopSeconds":900,"maxSessionSeconds":86400,"retainDays":30},"env":{},"labels":{}}`. 201 created, 200 when the alias already has one.
- `GET /v1/sandboxes?alias=user-23` - that one sandbox, or an empty page. `GET /v1/sandboxes?label=key=value&limit=100&cursor=` lists them.
- `GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}`
- `PATCH /v1/sandboxes/{id}` - `alias`, `imagePolicy`, `network`, `lifecycle`, `env`, `labels`; a network change applies to the running session at once, the rest from the next session. `imagePolicy` is `{"mode":"default"}`, `{"mode":"track","image":"<image without its tag>"}` or `{"mode":"pin","image":"<exact image>"}`, from `limits.images`.
- `POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/start`, `POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/stop`
- `DELETE /v1/sandboxes/{id}` - deletes the home and any published site too; there is no undo.

## Commands

- `POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/execs` - `{"shell":"npm test","cwd":"app","env":{},"timeoutSeconds":600,"stdin":false}` or `{"argv":["python3","main.py"]}`. Returns 201 with `id` at once. Send `Idempotency-Key` to make a retry safe.
- `GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/execs/{exec}?waitSeconds=30` - status and, when finished, `outcome`: `exited` with `exitCode` (and `reason` `oom_killed` or `pids_limited` when a limit explains it), `timed_out`, `cancelled`, or `interrupted` with `reason`.
- `GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/execs/{exec}/output?offset=0&waitSeconds=20&maxBytes=65536` - `{"frames":[{"kind":"stdout","text":"...","end":42}],"nextOffset":42,"complete":false}`. Loop with `offset = nextOffset` until `complete`; `maxBytes` bounds a page, which still carries at least one frame. Output is kept on the server: after a disconnect, resume from the last offset. With `Accept: text/event-stream` the same output arrives as server-sent events, ending with `event: end`.
- `POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/execs/{exec}/stdin?close=true` - raw bytes; only for execs started with `"stdin":true`.
- `POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/execs/{exec}/cancel`
- `GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/execs` - recent execs, newest first.

To run a command and wait for its result: start it, loop over `output` until `complete`, then read the
exec for its `outcome`.

## Publishing to the web

Only when the server has a pages role: `GET /v1/info` reports `"publishing": true`. Without one these
answer `not_implemented`.

- `POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/site` - `{"path":"dist"}`. Publishes a snapshot of that directory and returns `{"url","release","files","bytes","publishedAt"}`. The address is the server's: it is random, so it says nothing about the sandbox, and it stays the same every time you publish again. The URL is public: anyone with the link sees those files.
- `GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/site` - what this sandbox has published, or `not_found`.
- `DELETE /v1/sandboxes/{id}/site` - takes it down; the sandbox keeps its files. Publishing after that is a new site at a new address.

A site is a snapshot, not the live home: build first, then publish. Static files only - no server side
runs there. A file or directory whose name starts with a dot (`.git`, `.env`, `.well-known`) fails the
whole publish, and symlinks are skipped. One sandbox has one site, and deleting the sandbox takes it
down.

## Files

Paths are absolute or relative to `/home/sandbox`.

- `GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/files/content?path=notes/a.txt&maxBytes=1048576` - raw bytes; a file larger than `maxBytes` (optional) is refused with `payload_too_large` before any byte is sent.
- `PUT /v1/sandboxes/{id}/files/content?path=notes/a.txt` - raw bytes in the body; replaces atomically, creates parent directories.
- `GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/files/entries?path=notes` - directory listing.
- `GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/files/stat?path=notes/a.txt`
- `DELETE /v1/sandboxes/{id}/files?path=notes&recursive=true`

## Errors worth handling

- `capacity_exhausted` (503) and `unavailable` (503): retry after `Retry-After` seconds.
- `busy` (409): the sandbox already runs as many commands as allowed; wait for one to finish.
- `payload_too_large` (413): a file, body or site beyond its limit; `detail` names it.
- `insufficient_storage` (507): the home is full. Delete files from it before writing again.
- `invalid_request` (400): the `detail` member says what to fix.
- `not_found` (404): the sandbox, exec, file or site does not exist; `detail` says which. A missing sandbox comes back with `POST /v1/sandboxes`.
